title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Orphans and Vulnerable Children - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

description.narrative: PEPFAR: HIV/AIDS - Improve the lives of orphans and other vulnerable children and families affected by HIV/AIDS. Strengthen communities to meet the needs of orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, supporting community-based responses, helping children and adolescents to meet their own needs, creating a supportive social and policy environment. Activities could include training caregivers, increasing access to education, economic support, targeted food and nutrition support, and legal aid. Institutional responses would also be included. ARV treatment of children is excluded from this category and should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and Sub-Element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). Palliative care, including basic health care and support and TB/HIV prevention, management and treatment, as well as their related laboratory services and pharmaceuticals, when delivered within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under this aspect. Other health care associated with the continuum of HIV/AIDS illness, including HIV/TB services, when delivered outside a program for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.6 (Basic Health Care and Support) or Sub-Element 1.1.7 (TB/HIV). - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

(Uganda): USAID Uganda is contributing to Uganda's agriculture/agribusiness sector by improving the performance and competitiveness of the bean, coffee and maize value-chains through a co-operation agreement with the Royal Danish Embassy. These are the three focus-commodity value chains of the Uganda Mission's Feed the Future program. Activities are addressing the principal weaknesses in the three value chains by improving inputs supply and quality, production, internal and external marketing, storage, post-harvest handling and processing and financial services, to make the commodity value chains more competitive and better able to meet local, regional and international market standards. Results expected over this project's life are improved income and food security of up to 400,000 smallholder farming households, increased volume of traded agricultural produce, improved quality of coffee, maize and beans, the provision of new farming/agribusiness loans to some 35,000 clients, and enabling access by an expected 20,000 smallholder farmers to savings' facilities.

U-Growth (Uganda Growth) is a rural economic development programme focussing on growth and employment creation with agriculture and agribusiness at its core.The U-Growth programme has three components: 1. Public Sector Agriculture Support. Technical Assistance to the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries.2. Rural Transport Infrastructure. The component will through earmarked sector budget support be part of the rehabilitation of 3000 km. of district roads in Northern Uganda and a number of other community transport infrastructures. It will also support National Training at Mount Elgon Labour-based Training Centre and the Ministry of Works and Transport.3. The Agribusiness Initiative. The Initiative will support the Ugandan objective of strengthening the competitiveness of Ugandas agricultural and agro-processing sector, as a primary driver for growth and employment. It will apply value chain approaches, initially focusing on coffee, maize, oil seeds, pulses and export horticultural products.

title.narrative: Jinja Regional Referral Hospital (JRRH) Strengthening Project

description.narrative: (Uganda): JRRH is a government-to-government award that supports Uganda's Ministry of Health (MOH) to bridge the gap between the central and district levels of the health system. JRRH will enhance the oversight and coordination functions of the MOH at lower levels to maximize effectiveness and efficiency gains. FY 2022 nutrition and maternal and child health (MCH) funds will leverage PEPFAR support to this activity and build a regional platform for quality improvement in family planning service delivery and maternal, newborn, and child health services, including Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response. TB funds will strengthen drug resistance case management in the JRRH and improve TB treatment success rate to 90%. Nutrition, TB and MCH funds will contribute to cross-cutting Health Systems Support.JRRH will serve as a center of excellence for reproductive, family planning, maternal, neonatal, adolescent, and child health and nutrition services in 11 districts, while ensuring the reduction of gender-based violence and promotion of gender equality. JRRH will act as a regional capacity building hub and as a central platform for sustainable skills transfer to the lower-level health facilities.JRRH will prioritize: 1) implementing improved regional hospital-district patient referral and information flow; 2) data-driven decision making and knowledge management; 3) standardization of supportive supervision and policy dissemination; 4) quality assurance; and 5) district and regional level planning and coordination. JRRH will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence; 3) improve nutrition outcomes; and 4) build the capacity of health facilities to strengthen outreach and mobile clinics to ensure continuity of services during climate-related disruptions..

title.narrative: Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital (MRHH) Strengthening Project

description.narrative: (Uganda): MRRH is a government-to-government award that supports Uganda's efforts to bridge the gap between the central and district levels of the health system. MRRH will enhance oversight and coordination functions of the Ministry of Health to maximize effectiveness and efficiency. With FY 2022 nutrition, MCH, and TB funds, the activity will leverage PEPFAR support to build a regional platform for service delivery improvement and capacity building in lower-level health facilities. TB funding will strengthen drug resistance case management in the regional referral hospitals and improve the TB treatment success rate to 90%, as envisioned in the FY 2022 TB roadmap. Nutrition, MCH and TB funding will contribute to cross-cutting Health Systems Support.MRRH will prioritize improvement initiatives in the region and serve as a center of excellence for nutrition, TB, and maternal/neonatal/adolescent/child health services in the 11 districts in the Ankole region, while ensuring the reduction of gender-based violence and the promotion of gender equality. MRRH will act as a regional hub to coordinate capacity building in the region, and as a central platform for sustainable skills transfer to the lower level health facilities.MRRH will prioritize improving regional hospital-district patient referral and information flow; data-driven decision making; knowledge management; standardization of supportive supervision and policy dissemination; quality assurance; and district- and regional-level planning and coordination. MRRH will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence; 3) improve nutrition outcomes; and 4) build the capacity of health facilities to strengthen outreach and mobile clinics to ensure continuity of services during climate-related disruptions..

Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

title.narrative: Teacher Rotation and Student Outcomes: Experimental Evidence from Uganda

description.narrative: This project seeks to incentivize public school teachers in one Ugandan school district by rewarding instructors whose students improve their standardized test scores. Under this plan, the highest-performing teachers have the opportunity to transfer to the next teaching assignment of their choice, and many other high performers have that option as well.

title.narrative: PayDash: Improving Last-Mile Access to Information on Social Program Delivery

description.narrative: Indias Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provides rural households up to 100 days paid manual labor annually and is a critical social safety net. In 2019-20, more than 50 million households participated in MGNREGA with a 45 percent increase in program participation during the COVID-19 pandemic. When it functions well, MGNREGA stimulates economic activity and provides employment during agricultural downturns. However, workers wait an average of 53 days, or as many as 160 days, to receive payments, making it difficult to align income with expenses and incur debt. Delays also incentivize exploitation of marginalized people as local leaders often front payments to MGNREGA workers awaiting their wages, only to take a disproportionately large share in return once wages arrive. To better track payment processing through the bureaucracy, researchers partnered with Government of India officials and software programmers to develop a data dashboard called PayDash. PayDash is a free and user-friendly tool that tracks payment processing and approvals throughout the bureaucratic chain, making key information more accessible, clear, and actionable so government officials can immediately find the cause of and address delays. A randomized controlled trial (RCT) in Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand showed that the use of PayDash among bureaucrats significantly reduced delays for MGNREGAs 7.7 million workers. The implementing partner is conducting an RCT in Bihar to test whether information provision to elected officials as well as bureaucrats increases PayDashs effectiveness for the states 4.7 million MGNREGA participants. The implementing partner will complete the ongoing Bihar RCT, update the PayDash platform, and train government officials and technology staff to use and maintain PayDash, which will enable it to scale sustainably. This study will provide critical evidence on how PayDash can be deployed most effectively as it expands to o

title.narrative: Evaluating the Lively Minds Early Childhood Care and Education Program

description.narrative: A large scale randomized control trial (RCT) is being conducted of a program that supports quality pre-school education in Ghana and Uganda, the intervention seeks to improve childrens health, cognitive and socio-emotional development, and their home and school environments. It trains volunteer women from local villages to run weekly, hour-long play sessions in which children participate in fun, interactive games that strengthen their cognitive, language, and social and emotional skills. It also encourages handwashing and provides monthly parenting courses that teach caregivers simple ways to improve home-based care, including nutrition, hygiene, and malaria prevention.

title.narrative: Measuring the Impact of Information: Evaluating the 3-2-1 Service

description.narrative: To collect evidence on the efficacy of information systems, Viamo is testing its 3-2-1 Information Service, which delivers free, expert-approved messages to 30 million mobile phone users across 18 countries on a variety of topics, including agriculture, education, and health. These on-demand messages use human-centered design to increase users' understanding of vital information. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, Viamo will develop new content for the 3-2-1 Service and run a large-scale randomized controlled trial in Uganda to explore the impact of this behavior change technology within the context of maternal health and family planning.

title.narrative: Piloting a Neonatal Advanced Life Support Program

description.narrative: Since 1990, global neonatal mortality has significantly decreased due to medical training advances. While Ethiopia has halved neonatal mortality, its rate is still ten times higher than the global average of high-income countries. The Golden Minutethe first minute of life after birthis critical, especially in addressing neonatal asphyxiation (the inability to breathe at birth). To reduce neonatal asphyxiation, the implementing partner will apply lessons from international standard health worker training programs to design a new, enhanced training program called the Neonatal Advanced Life Support program. The implementing partners low-dose, high-frequency model balances time spent on training and knowledge transfer with skills practice and follow-up training. Following a promising pilot, Ethiopias Ministry of Health expressed interest in adopting and scaling the enhanced program, pending a more extensive study. The implementing partner will test its training program in seven medical facilities in Addis Ababa to determine its relative effectiveness in less-resourced medical facilities. If it proves effective across facilities, the training program has the potential to reduce neonatal mortality across 22,000 annual deliveries and inform a planned scale-up to 14 regional health centers.

title.narrative: Scaling Up Access to Green, Clean Public Transport in Rwanda Program

description.narrative: The purpose of the scaling up access to clean, green public transport in Rwanda program is to transition buses from diesel to electric buses.

title.narrative: Testing a Combined SIT/IIT Approach to Control Mosquito-Borne Diseases at Scale

description.narrative: Mosquito-borne diseases cause suffering for hundreds of millions of people and claim more than 700,000 lives yearly. Diseases such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya cause symptoms similar to malaria and are endemic in many parts of the world, yet there are no treatments for them nor vaccines for Zika and chikungunya. Mosquito control, particularly of the Aedes aegypti species, is seen as a potentially effective solution to slow or stop the spread of these diseases but has not yet demonstrated significant, sustainable impacts on disease transmission. Other than the application of toxic pesticides, there are currently two main forms of mosquito control: Sterile Insect Technique (SIT), where males are sterilized using radiation, and Incompatible Insect Technique (IIT), where males are infected with the Wolbachia bacteria, leaving wild females unable to reproduce when they mate. Neither technique has any negative human health effects; Wolbachia naturally occurs in insects but is not dangerous to humans. Individually, these strategies show promising results in suppressing the mosquito population, but neither has been shown to control mosquito-borne diseases sufficiently. However, SIT and IIT can potentially complement each other. Researchers from Michigan State University (MSU), in partnership with the Universidad Autnoma de Yucatn (UADY), are now testing this combined approach in Mexicos Yucatn Peninsula. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, MSU will implement this bundled approach and measure changes in mosquito population density and the prevalence of mosquito-borne diseases in humans. This investment builds on past USAID support through the Combating Zika and Future Threats Grand Challenge, which partially funded the UADY mosquito mass-rearing facility in 2016. title.narrative: Regional Health Integration to Enhance Services in North Acholi (RHITES-NA)

description.narrative: (Uganda): Although portions of the HIV and TB portfolio will transition to a local partner in FY 2021, RHITES-N, Acholi will continue to support the implementation of evidence-based integrated maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH); family planning (FP); nutrition interventions; and water, hygiene, and sanitation (WASH) interventions in eight districts with a total population of 1.5 million people. With $2,341,515 million in FY 2021 funds, four areas will be prioritized: consolidating high-impact, evidence-based interventions; strengthening community-level interventions to increase demand and uptake of quality health services; health system strengthening to improve health services; and strengthening health information systems including data collection, completeness, and utilization. To ensure safe implementation of USAID funded MNCH, FP, TB, nutrition, and WASH services during the COVID-19 pandemic, RHITES-N, Acholi will integrate intervention for prevention and management of COVID-19 including vaccine rollout and infection prevention and control based on Ugandan Ministry of Health guidelines. The Activity will also support targeted provision of personal protective equipment for service providers and beneficiaries of MNCH, FP, TB, and nutrition services. .RHITES-N, Acholi will engage with all stakeholders and beneficiaries to identify, plan, and implement local solutions to health challenges. RHITES-N, Acholi will promote commitment and capacity to provide high-quality health services..

description.narrative: (Uganda): USAID strives to increase household and community access to improved sanitation and water services; promote the adoption and expansion of key hygiene behaviors in homes, schools, and health facilities (in partnership with Rotary International); and strengthen district water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) governance for sustainable services.With FY 2022 funds, the Uganda Sanitation for Health Activity (USHA) will implement activities in 21 districts, with priority in northern districts. Activities will include expanding access to improved sanitation through the market-based sanitation implementation approach, community-led total sanitation and verification of open defecation free communities, and expanding community water access through implementing a pro-poor strategy. USHA will consolidate its social and behavior change campaign and strengthen fecal sludge management business models by establishing better market connections. USHA will provide technical assistance for the district-led national rollout of market-based sanitation and continue to consolidate capacity-building for districts in aspects of planning, information and data management, advocacy, and coordination. School WASH interventions will focus on completing infrastructure improvements and promoting WASH-friendly performance. At a national level, USHA will support the Government of Uganda (GOU) to implement the National Sanitation Marketing Guidelines to facilitate increased private sector participation in achieving universal basic sanitation in priority populations. USHA will also document and disseminate key learnings to national level stakeholders to inform the scale-up of appropriate and workable implementation approaches.USHA's interventions will support the GOU's COVID-19 response through facilitating improved water access, uptake of key behavior practices like handwashing, and infection prevention and control in households, communities, and institutions..

description.narrative: (Uganda): .The Integrated Community Agriculture and.Nutrition (ICAN) activity works with community groups to maximize economic.opportunities for vulnerable households, stabilize access to and.consumption of nutritious diets, and increase social capital by reinforcing.relationships among formal governance systems and communities. Through.collaboration with the private sector and district and local governments, and.increasing the organizational capacity of partnering organizations, ICAN is.laying the foundation for increased self-reliance in Uganda...With FY 2021.funds, ICAN will scale-up its work with community groups to promote resilience..ICAN's mother care groups and adolescent girls' camps will be scaled-up, and.participants will continue to receive family planning and nutrition.interventions. The mother care groups will be linked to Business Service.Providers for training in various enterprises e.g., tailoring, hairdressing and.agricultural enterprises. Diversification of income sources will help the.groups withstand climate-related and other shocks and stresses and increase.their resilience. All ICAN groups will be encouraged to plant multipurpose.trees to curb climate variability, and to use energy saving stoves to minimize.deforestation and associated climate impacts. In hilly areas in the South West,.households will be taught and encouraged to practice terracing and other.climate-smart farming techniques. ICAN will continue to collaborate with health.activities to advance a social and behavioral change curriculum...ICAN will.increase community mobilization by facilitating community members' civil.society engagement to improve their access to health and social protection.services. ICAN will enhance economic opportunities for 116,000 poor households.by improving livelihoods and strengthening connections to markets and financial.services. Participating communities will have stronger networks and services.and be better positioned to respond to shocks..

title.narrative: Promoting Peaceful Coexistence and Resilience Activity in Northern Uganda

description.narrative: Targeted post conflict communities are living together in harmony & enjoy good mental health.The activity targets 14,400 households and families in both Lango and Acholi regions. Each target household benefits from three core interventions: 1) peace building, 2) trauma healing and psychosocial support, 3) economic empowerment.Strengthen the role of traditional support structures in use of consensus-based dispute resolution and building their capacity to deal with drivers of all forms of violence and harmful practices. Provide Mental Health & Psychosocial Support Services that improve the social functioning of conflict affected households through the provision of psychosocial care, and trauma support. Empower conflict affected households through socioeconomic initiatives that minimizes their risk of relapse. Strengthen the roles of the existing referral networks that enhances project sustainability.

(Uganda): The ERP Hardware activity consists primarily of hardware procurement, installation, training of the National Medical Store (NMS) staff on the ERP technologies, and maintenance of equipment. The ERP hardware activity will install a primary data center at NMS central and a disaster recovery site in a government data center in Jinja. The activity will also support the relocation of the primary data center to the new NMS warehouse currently being built. Implementation of the ERP will create an integrated and interoperable system with a supply chain focus on several functions. The ERP hardware is implemented in tandem with the ERP software. This activity will receive $345,000 in FY 2020 resources to help decentralize the ERP system to Health Center IIIs, which will help improve transparency for ordering and monitoring commodities at the facility-level.. ..

The purpose of this contract is to support USAID Uganda strengthen overall collaborating, learning and adapting (CLA) performance in order to, in turn, enhance program impact to accelerate USAID s transition out of foreign assistance in Uganda.

description.narrative: (Uganda): Providing USAID commodities through the National Medical Stores (NMS) has provided the agency with the opportunity to help optimize NMS' supply chain system as it fulfills its mandate to procure, warehouse, and distribute commodities to the public sector. The Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Software has recently been procured and installed at NMS. This activity will receive $250,000 in FY 2021 funding to provide national level supply chain system support and subnational roll out of the system. The activity will receive additional support from PEPFAR that is not captured in the OP. Successful implementation of the ERP software will ensure accountability for public health commodities, which include reproductive health, family planning, and malaria commodities, and will strengthen national systems for improved supply chain management. The activity will continue to integrate the ERP package that incorporates all supply chain management data for NMS. .

(Uganda): With FY 2022 Malaria, MCH, FP and Nutrition funds, UHSS will: 1) improve leadership and accountability for health sector results; 2) increase availability and improve management of health system resources; and 3) strengthen community systems for quality health services. The focus will shift to addressing HSS barriers to improving Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health/Malaria and HIV activities..UHSS will support the Ministry of Health (MOH) to integrate the National Community Engagement and Social Protection strategy into broader health policy. UHSS will collaborate with service delivery partners to finalize the Community Health Extension Worker Pilot. UHSS will work with the MOH to improve data visibility at community service delivery points.UHSS will support human resources for health (HRH) and their MOH advisors will address gaps in public financial management, and monitor the use of external project funds. UHSS will work with local government facilities to improve financial planning and funding for primary health care. UHSS will support the MOH and regional referral hospitals to improve skills in telementoring, and support supervision. It will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address its impact; 3) improve nutrition outcomes; 4) improve access and utilization of micronutrients; and 5) improve access and utilization of vitamin A.Specific activities to reduce climate risks to health will include providing budget advocacy support to the MOH to plan for contingency resources for procurement of additional essential health commodities that may be required due to seasonal outbreak of diseases like diarrhea and pneumonia. UHSS will support priority districts to include contingency plans in their annual work plans to reduce climate risks to health....

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Inclusive Agricultural Markets Activity (IAM) works with agro-industry, the Government of Uganda (GOU), and private sector organizations to improve the agriculture market system. It works in the Global Food Security Strategy zones of influence, Karamoja, and the refugee-hosting districts.The Activity will use FY 2022 funds to: 1) improve access to high-quality agricultural products and services through strengthening input distribution networks and reducing counterfeit goods; 2) strengthen supply chains to help ensure effective movement of goods and services; 3) work with traders, exporters, millers, and processors to upgrade post-harvest handling, logistics, conditioning and storage, and manufacturing of commodities; 4) work with agro and food processors to improve the quality and nutritional value of food products; 5) build the capacity of small and medium food processors around food safety and quality standards, fortification and micro-nutrient enhancement, and food handling processes; and 6) support the seed systems market by engaging with farmer groups to produce high-quality declared seeds for nutrient dense beans and pulses.The Activity will also: 1) work with the GOU to improve the policy and regulatory framework for quality standards for agricultural products, managing counterfeits, and controlling aflatoxins in grains; 2) support service providers, including financial institutions, to supply affordable loans and insurance products; 3) strengthen the capacity of business development service providers to provide market and weather information and extension services; and 4) support farmer organizations and agribusinesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic to recover and become more resilient. The Activity will use funds to scale up interventions in Karamoja and refugee hosting districts (the resilience zone), and leverage private sector investments to build the capacity of agribusinesses and farmer organizations to engage in market activities...

(Uganda): With FY 2022 funds, SCENE will deepen engagement, debate, and consensus on constitutional, political, and legal reforms. SCENE will engage citizens to increase trust of, and constructive engagement with, the public sector agencies charged with legislation and the implementation of constitutional and electoral reforms. .SCENE will directly engage key Government of Uganda (GOU) actors, including Parliament, the Electoral Commission, and local law enforcement, to reduce political fragility in a country that has never seen a peaceful transition of power. SCENE will bring together electoral civil society organizations to conduct joint strategic planning, and engage and partner with GOU counterparts to support freer, more peaceful political engagement in Uganda..

title.narrative: USAID/Uganda Maternal Child Health and Nutrition (MCHN) Activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): MCHN will use FY 2022 MCH, FP, and Nutrition funds to support integrated, multi-sectoral maternal, newborn, and child health (MCH) and nutrition interventions cutting across the portfolio. MCHN will strengthen the Government of Uganda's performance in implementing strategies to improve MCH; water, sanitation, and hygiene; and nutrition outcomes. MCHN will contribute to health system strengthening to ensure services are accessible and affordable for all. It will focus specifically on governance and leadership, human resources for health, and data use at the national level. The key outcomes expected include: 1) improved rollout and uptake of priority MCH and nutrition strategies; 2) strengthened quality of MCH and nutrition services; 3) increased use of data to improve service delivery; 4) strengthened cooperation and coordination; and 5) good governance and leadership at national and regional levels to drive improved MCH and nutrition outcomes.MCHN will strengthen the integration and scale-up of immediate postpartum family planning during the postnatal period. It will strengthen the scale-up of key behavior change related to WASH and increased access to safe sanitation services within the health facilities. It will continue to ensure that the support provided is responsive to programming within the COVID context. It will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence; 3) improve nutrition outcomes; 4) improve access and utilization of micronutrients; 5) improve access and utilization of vitamin A; and 6) improve WASH related outcomes at the household and facility level in implementation districts. By strengthening resilient health systems at national and sub-national level, the activity will respond to climate related service delivery disruptions..

title.narrative: Program for Accelerated Control of TB in Karamoja (PACT Karamoja)

description.narrative: (Uganda): The PACT Karamoja activity will improve TB case detection rates in the Karamoja region from the current rate of 75 percent to 85 percent, and treatment success rates from the current rate of 48 percent to 90 percent. This activity will directly contribute to the National TB Control Program's goal of reducing the TB incidence from 201 cases per 100,000 persons to 117 cases per 100,000 persons by 2025-26. This will be achieved through the implementation and scale-up of evidence-based community and facility interventions across the TB diagnostic, prevention, and treatment cascade. With FY 2022 funds, priority interventions include: 1) strengthening community TB case finding through community sensitization and engagement; 2) improving linkages between communities and health facilities; 3) scaling up contact tracing approaches; 4) addressing socio-cultural barriers to accessing TB treatment and prevention service; 5) improving the quality of TB diagnostic and treatment services at the facility-level; and 5) scaling up differentiated service delivery models for TB service delivery. This activity will contribute to the achievement of the End TB targets for epidemic control. PACT Karamoja will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services, and activities that prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence. By working closely with community partners including Village Health Team (VHT) in increasing health seeking behavior, the activity will mitigate service disruption as a result of climatic conditions. .

(Uganda): FPA engages with the Government of Uganda to strengthen the capacity of local institutions and communities to increase the adoption of positive reproductive health behaviors. With FY 2022 funding, FPA will strengthen the national family planning (FP) program and health system to create an enabling environment to address key barriers to adopting healthy reproductive practices. FPA will work with ten local and community-based partners to build evidence-based, high-impact practices and design and implement strategies that address the underlying social, cultural, and structural barriers to FP access.FPA's interventions primarily focus on demand generation, reporting, and service delivery. At the national level, activities focus on improving accountable leadership, sustainable financing, health workforce, and information systems management. FPA will contribute to the development of a national, multi-sectoral plan to implement the FP2030 commitments. FPA will target women and men of reproductive age, focusing on adolescents and youth under 25. FPA will support service delivery in 11 districts in Uganda. It will ensure that FP commodities are accessible, affordable, and appropriate. It will enhance the capacity of leaders and health care providers through training, mentorship, performance assessment, and recognition. FPA will engage communities, adolescents, and youth as co-creators of gender and youth responsive services that identify and address the root causes of the entrenched social norms and behaviors. FPA will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) prevent gender-based violence and address its impact; 3) engage the private sector to increase access to high quality family planning services; and 4) mitigate the impact of climate induced disruptions by strengthening resilient health systems at national and sub-national level...

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Combating Wildlife Crime Activity aims to reduce wildlife crime and trafficking. Building on lessons learned and complementing other ongoing biodiversity conservation activities, FY 2022 funds will be used to: 1) strengthen wildlife protection and the leadership skills and capacity of law enforcement personnel; 2) improve cooperation and data-sharing among government institutions, civil society, and the private sector to improve enforcement; and 3) promote data-driven conservation approaches through research, analysis, and information management. The Activity will coordinate closely with the Mission's flagship Accountability activity to enhance transparency and build partnerships to combat wildlife crime-related corruption..

(Uganda): The Biodiversity for Resilience Activity will strengthen engagement in biodiversity protection among private sector actors, protected area managers, communities, and civil society. It will promote sustainable conservation and build resilient ecosystems around priority protected areas, including lakes, national parks, and forest reserves.With FY 2022 funds, the Activity will improve the governance and management of community conservancy areas, and develop conservation enterprises, including nature-based tourism. FY 2022 funds will be used to support protection of Budongo and Kalinzu Central Forest Reserves, which are important habitats for chimpanzees. These efforts will improve the management of protected areas and buffer zones, increase conservation-based economic growth, reduce poaching and retaliatory killing of wildlife and trade in wildlife products, and support the development and implementation of the regulations and guidelines required by the 2019 Wildlife Act. These efforts will also create investment opportunities for U.S. firms, advance American national security interests, and position Uganda as a destination for sustainable tourism.The activity will contribute to GEEA Fund Priority 3: securing women's economic future through green jobs and building resilience to climate change, through promoting conservation enterprises that provide income opportunities and support women to diversify their livelihoods. The activity will address climate risks and impacts by supporting climate-smart, organic and/or restorative agriculture practices in the buffer zones....

description.narrative: (Uganda): USAID's Uganda Biodiversity Fund (UBF) Activity aims to ensure that the Fund is a reputable, well-functioning, and sustainable conservation trust fund that is responsive to Uganda's conservation and natural resources management financing needs. UBF's mission is to catalyze, mobilize, and manage financial resources for biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of natural resources in Uganda..The Activity will use FY 2022 funds to: 1) further build UBF into an effective and efficient national conservation trust fund; 2) implement a grants program, including using funds mobilized from the private sector and other donors, to deliver impactful conservation in Uganda; and 3) strengthen partnerships and coordination among national and local actors that support locally-led, sustainable development..

(Uganda): With FY 2022 MCH and FP funds, the Civil Society Strengthening Activity (CSSA) improves the ability of Ugandan Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to influence and contribute to development outcomes in targeted sectors, including health; agriculture; food security; and democracy, human rights, and governance.The Activity provides technical assistance to strengthen the advocacy capacity of CSOs to influence policies across the sectors of health and HIV/AIDS, family planning, child and maternal health, agriculture and democracy. The Civil Society Strengthening activity will provide support to civil society organizations (CSOs) across the Mission's portfolio to increase cross-sector cooperation, strengthen cohesiveness and improve linkages to government. This integrated activity will advance Mission priorities in health, education, and economic growth. Interventions will include expanding the voice of local CSOs within networks, increasing their capacity to express interests; supporting civil society and media to partner effectively with local government; and strengthening the organizational capacity of CSOs for policy analysis and oversight, advocacy, coalition building, internal governance, and membership representation. CSSA will also fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services, and activities that prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence...

title.narrative: Local Partner Health Services – Kigezi and Lango

description.narrative: (Uganda): LPHS Kigezi and Lango is implemented by the Joint Clinical Research Center and supports a population of 3.4 million across six districts in Kigezi and nine districts in the Lango region. With FY 2022 TB funds, this activity will support the following TB activities: 1) screening and detection of all forms of TB in infants, children, and adults at facility and community levels; 2) early initiation and completion of anti-TB treatment for all patients diagnosed with all forms of TB; 3) ensuring strong community systems to strengthen the continuum of TB prevention, screening, diagnosis, care, and treatment; 4) improving the quality of the multi-drug resistant TB program and TB/HIV collaborative activities through the implementation and scale-up of evidence-based community and facility interventions across the TB diagnostic, prevention, and treatment cascade.To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, LPHS Kigezi and Lango will integrate infection prevention and control activities and support targeted provision of personal protective equipment, to protect service providers and beneficiaries of TB services. LPHS Kigezi and Lango will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services. By working closely with community partners including Village Health Teams (VHT) in increasing health seeking behavior, the activity will mitigate service disruption as a result of climatic conditions.Health systems strengthening activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds, and therefore, this activity is co-funded with HIV/PEPFAR funds for the HSS cross-cutting areas at subnational level.....

title.narrative: Local Partner Health Services - Ankole and Acholi Regions

description.narrative: (Uganda): This activity was awarded to the AIDS Support Organization (TASO) and supports a population of four million across twelve districts in Ankole and eight districts in Acholi. With FY 2022 TB funds, the Ankole and Acholi Region TB and HIV activity will prioritize the following areas: 1) screening and detection of all forms of TB in infants, children, and adults at facility and community levels; 2) early initiation and completion of anti-TB treatment for all patients diagnosed with all forms of TB; 3) ensuring strong community systems to strengthen the continuum of TB prevention, screening, diagnosis, care, and treatment; and 4) improving the quality of the multi-drug resistant TB program and TB/HIV collaborative activities through the implementation and scale-up of evidence-based community and facility interventions across the TB diagnostic, prevention, and treatment cascade.To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, the activity in the Ankole and Acholi regions will integrate infection prevention and control to protect service providers and beneficiaries of TB services. LPHS Acholi and Ankole will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services. By working closely with community partners including Village Health Teams (VHT) in increasing health seeking behavior, the activity will mitigate service disruption as a result of climatic conditions.Health systems strengthening activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds, and therefore, this activity is co-funded with HIV/PEPFAR funds for the HSS cross-cutting areas at subnational level..

title.narrative: Local Service Delivery for HIV/AIDS Activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): LSDA is implemented by the Uganda Protestant Medical Bureau (UPMB) and supports all the faith-based health facilities across the country. With FY 2022 TB funds, LSDA will support the following TB activities: 1) screening and detection of all forms of TB in infants, children, and adults at facility and community levels; 2) early initiation and completion of anti-TB treatment for all patients diagnosed with all forms of TB; 3) ensuring strong community systems to strengthen the continuum of TB prevention, screening, diagnosis, care, and treatment; and 4) improving the quality of the multi-drug resistant TB program and the TB/HIV collaborative activities via the implementation and scale-up of evidence-based community and facility interventions across the TB diagnostic, prevention, and treatment pathway. LSDA will also contribute to Health System Strengthening activities, including improved governance and coordination, commodities security and human resources for health.To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, LSDA will integrate infection prevention and control activities and support targeted provision of personal protective equipment to protect service providers and beneficiaries of TB services. LSDA will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services and activities to mitigate the impact of climate induced disruptions to the delivery of health services.Health systems strengthening activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds...

title.narrative: Domestic Resource Mobilization for Development Activity (DRM4D)

description.narrative: The goal of the DRM4D activity is to increase domestic revenue mobilization (both tax and non-tax) and thereby create the fiscal space for public spending and investments in service delivery and other priority areas. The activity will support interventions that enhance predictability and fairness in the tax system, reduce the costs and burdens of tax compliance, and create platforms and opportunities for public-private dialogue on both the mobilization and use of public resources. At the sub-national level, the activity will support interventions aimed at expanding tax and non-tax revenue options for selected local governments. The project will also engage with the Government of Uganda (GOU) on opportunities for investing the increased revenue into poverty reducing sectors such as health, education and agriculture.

(Uganda): The Health Care Waste Management (HCWM) activity will be implemented by Green Label Services Limited (GLSL), a local Ugandan-owned hazardous waste management firm. The activity will be funded with $400,000 in FY 2021 and will use a health systems strengthening approach to remediate the potential human health and environmental impacts of maternal, newborn, child health, and family planning related hazardous health care waste, through safe and proper segregation, collection, storage, transportation, treatment, and disposal. This activity will be conducted in accordance with the National Environmental Management Authority, the Ministry of Health, and USAID's environment compliance standards. The HCWM activity will also provide technical assistance to selected health facilities so they become models of excellence for HCWM practices and can be emulated by other health facilities during the life of the activity. .

title.narrative: Housing Modification Study and Enhanced Entomological Surveillance Activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): HMS & EES is implementing a two-phase study evaluating epidemiological and entomological effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, feasibility, and acceptability of housing modification in Uganda to reduce malaria infection. Despite the gaps in evidence, improved housing shows promise for reducing malaria transmission. This study will explore housing modification as a malaria control intervention and assess the degree to which it may offer protection in moderate to high malaria endemicity settings. The first phase of the study was successfully completed and identified the two best interventions (partial screening and eave tubes) to conduct a randomized control trial for two years (2022 and 2023)..With FY 2022 funds, the study will continue the cohort follow up and expand the understanding of the impact of housing modification on malaria. HMS & EES will fund activities that prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence..

title.narrative: Karamoja Resilience Support Unit II (KRSU II)

description.narrative: (Uganda): The goal of the Karamoja Resilience Support Unit-II (KRSU II) activity is to support the Government of Uganda (GOU) to plan and coordinate development projects in the Karamoja region to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of development assistance. With FY 2022 funds, KRSU II will analyze existing studies and strategies; conduct assessments on emerging development challenges and opportunities in Karamoja; and disseminate new evidence from studies focused on agriculture, natural resource management, and nutrition-related social behavior changes, amongst others, to the GOU, donors, partners, USAID, and other stakeholders to inform and guide improved development planning and service delivery in the Karamoja sub-region.KRSU II will facilitate coordination of the GOU, development partners, and agencies providing humanitarian assistance in Karamoja to network, and identify areas for collective action. KRSU will continue to provide organizational and technical support for coordination structures, such as the Health and Nutrition and Social Behavior Change working groups, amongst others. KRSU II will also assist the GOU's Ministry for Karamoja Affairs to better coordinate with district and sub-county leadership to operationalize the Karamoja Integrated Development Plan, guide investments, and share development results. KRSU II will enhance the GOU's coordination capacity to eventually assume the role in the future..

description.narrative: (Uganda): The purpose of the Rights and Justice Activity (RAJA) is to increase citizens' ability to exercise their rights and enjoy their fundamental freedoms in a safe and secure manner, and ensure that victims of human rights abuses have access to justice, protection, and referral services. This activity will focus on advancing three objectives:.Objective 1 - Advocacy: Individuals and organizations defend and maintain the legislative frameworks that enable civic and political activism and ensure access to justice, particularly for children..Objective 2 - Physical Security, Digital Security, and Compliance Support: Individuals and organizations exercising civil and political rights do so more safely and securely in the face of physical, digital, and legal threats..Objective 3 - Legal Aid and Social Services for Victims: Vulnerable populations such as human rights defenders, women, children, youth, LGBTI, and people with disabilities whose rights are violated can access legal remedies and social services...

(Uganda): The Feed the Future Institutional and Systems Strengthening Activity will build the capacity and systems of key national-level inistries, departments and agencies (MDAs) and industry apex organizations (IAOs) that are vital to driving agricultural sector growth, including improving the safety of food supply across agriculture value chains. The Activity will support these entities to improve their internal processes, enabling them to better fulfill their mandates. The Activity will focus on key entry points within the MDAs' and IAOs' structures and systems to optimize functionality, inclusiveness, and adoption of innovative approaches to spur agriculture sector development, including increased production, quality, and safety of food important for nutrition.With FY 2022 funds, activities will include public-private sector dialogue to bring about desired reforms and encourage participation in policy implementation. These activities will promote behavioral change in selected MDAs and IAOs through: 1) ongoing institutional self-assessments and implementation of improvement action plans, 2) platforms for collaboration among market actors, 3) capacity building for strategic communication, 4) human resource capacity development, and 5) uptake of digital solutions for efficient service delivery. The Activity will also deploy grants as a tool to incentivize adoption of innovative business models and approaches to service delivery among the IAOs and MDAs.The activity will contribute to the Gender Equity and Equality Action (GEEA) Fund Priority 5: Dismantling systemic barriers through building the capacity of ministries, departments, agencies, and industry apex organizations to carry out gender responsive planning, programming, and budgeting. It will support the development, review, and implementation of gender strategies at the National Meteorological Authority; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives; and the Equal Opportunities Commission...

(Uganda): The USAID-funded Feed the Future Strategic Investments Activity works to accelerate, catalyze, and unlock additional investment in the agriculture, productive use of energy, and health sectors. The Activity supports private sector enterprises to be investor-ready, secure loan guarantees to lower transaction costs and risks, and develop partnerships that unlock commercial investments. FY 2022 resources will fund transaction advisory services to at least 23 deals to make them investment ready. FY 2022 funding will be used to provide advisory services, hold financing matchmaking events, conduct investment analyses, and design a virtual deal room to support pre-financial close negotiations between investors and investee projects in Uganda. FY 2022 funds will support private-sector-led innovation that increases the productive use of electricity by agricultural small- and medium-sized enterprises, farmer cooperatives, and farmers. The Activity will facilitate viable, commercially-driven local and international private sector investments that align with USAID's development objectives. For example, the majority of investments target the agricultural sector to increase agricultural production, improve food safety through post-harvest processing and storage, and increase the diversity of crops available to improve nutrition. Over its lifetime, the Activity will mobilize $140 million in private capital to Uganda while improving the livelihoods of 100,000 underrepresented and marginalized people.The Activity will contribute to the Gender Equity and Equality Action (GEEA) Fund priority 4: Promote entrepreneurship, and financial and digital inclusion, through investing in 12% women-owned enterprises, that together will seek $29 million in financing. The activity further will provide advisory services, facilitate access to relevant information and engage women-led and -owned businesses who receive business development support...

title.narrative: Local Partner Health Services - East Central

description.narrative: (Uganda): LPHS East Central was awarded to a local organization and supports TB and HIV interventions in 12 districts in the East Central region of Uganda, serving a population of approximately four million people. With FY 2022 TB funds, the activity will prioritize the following areas: 1) screening and detection of all forms of TB in infants, children, and adults at facility and community levels; 2) early initiation and completion of anti-TB treatment for all patients diagnosed with all forms of TB; 3) ensuring strong community systems to strengthen the continuum of TB prevention, screening, diagnosis, care, and treatment; and 4) improving the quality of the multi-drug resistant TB program and TB/HIV collaborative activities through the implementation and scale-up of evidence-based community and facility interventions across the TB diagnostic, prevention, and treatment cascade.The priority interventions will include: 1) strengthening community TB case finding through community sensitization and engagement; 2) improving linkages between communities and health facilities; 3) scaling up contact tracing approaches; and 4) addressing socio-cultural barriers to accessing TB treatment and prevention services.To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, the activity will integrate infection prevention and control activities and support targeted provision of personal protective equipment to protect service providers and beneficiaries of TB services. LPHS EC will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services. By working closely with community partners including Village Health Teams (VHT) in increasing health seeking behavior, the activity will mitigate service disruption as a result of climatic conditions.These activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds, and therefore, this activity is co-funded with HIV/PEPFAR funds for the HSS cross-cutting areas at subnational level...

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Malaria Reduction Activity (MRA) strengthens the capacity of the Ministry of Health's National Malaria Control Division and District Health Management Teams through a package of high-impact malaria interventions focused on community prevention and case management in high burden areas. These include distributing and promoting use of long-lasting insecticide treated nets during antenatal care, prevention of malaria during pregnancy, strengthening of diagnostics and treatment of malaria, social and behavior change, capacity strengthening, surveillance, operational research (for the Therapeutic Efficacy Test), and reporting. These aim to decrease malaria morbidity and mortality in 53 target districts in Busoga, Karamoja, West Nile, Lango, and Acholi. The Activity will protect approximately 13 million people from the effects of malaria.MRA will prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence. It will fund specific activities to reduce climate risks including support to Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWS) and Village Health Teams (VHTs) to provide integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) of malaria in target districts, some of which are flood-prone and likely to face health service delivery disruptions during floods and other natural disasters associated with climate change. MRA will provide funding to CHEWS and VHTs to conduct home to home visits and through interpersonal communication with household members, encourage removal of mosquito vector breeding grounds such as stagnant water and overall encourage proper household sanitation. MRA will include disaster preparedness, sanitation, and social behavior change activities aimed at reducing or mitigating climate risks to health in their annual work plans...

(Uganda): HCWM will be implemented by a local Ugandan-owned hazardous waste management firm. With FY 2022 MCH and FP funds, HCWM will use a health systems strengthening approach to remediate the potential human health and environmental impacts of maternal, newborn, child health, and family planning related hazardous health care waste through safe and proper segregation, collection, storage, transportation, treatment, and disposal. This activity will be conducted in accordance with the National Environmental Management Authority, the Ministry of Health Waste Management guidelines, and USAID's environment compliance standards. The activity will support facilities to properly manage health care waste when they carry out outreaches and mobile clinics during service disruptions caused by climatic conditions..

description.narrative: (Uganda): With FY 2022 funds, Local Partner Health Services-TB will provide technical assistance to the National TB and HIV programs and support management of multidrug resistant TB (MDR-TB) across 17 treatment sites nationwide. It will also increase TB/HIV case detection and improve TB treatment outcomes through a health systems strengthening approach in the regions of Kampala, Wakiso, and Mukono.The activity will provide technical assistance to USAID implementing partners and focus districts to reduce Uganda's TB burden and contribute to the U.S. Government and World Health Organization's End TB Strategy, which seeks to end the TB epidemic by 2035. The activity works directly with Ministry of Health leadership to address Uganda's high TB burden and focuses on finding missing TB cases through effective community and facility-based interventions.The activity will partner with other USG-supported TB/HIV partners. Coordination includes: 1) providing support to the National TB Leprosy program to improve the quality of the current MDR-TB program; 2) developing and implementing strategies that mitigate impact of COVID-19; 3) increasing screening and detection of all forms of TB; 4) improving early treatment initiation and successful treatment completion; and 5) strengthening community systems to support the continuum of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.LPHS-TB will fund activities to: 1) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; 2) improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services; and 3) prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence and activities to mitigate the impact of climate induced disruptions to the delivery of health services.These activities are jointly supported with PEPFAR (HIV) funds, and therefore, this activity is co-funded with HIV/PEPFAR funds for the HSS cross-cutting areas at subnational level...

usaid local priorities & partnerships activity (lppa) intends to partner with ugandan local organizations to improve the ways that local groups work on a regional level to assess, plan, and build development alliances. the local priorities and partnership activity (lppa) is a usaid-funded activity that will support ugandan regional organizations to achieve this objective. lppa will ensure there are reputable, inclusive, functional, and sustainable regional platforms to pursue sound, evidence-informed, and scalable development approaches and initiatives. activity goals and purpose: the goal of this activity is to develop the regional platforms into reputable, inclusive, functional, and sustainable entities that are capable of pursuing sound, evidence-informed, large-scale, and regional-centered development approaches and initiatives. activity purpose: the activity purpose is to work with local ugandan implementing partners that will support the regional platforms in their work with stakeholders and research partners. lppa will ensure ugandan organizations like the regional platforms have the capacity to operate independently and sustainably, and lppa will render support that enhances their organizational, leadership, technical, and administrative abilities. activity-level expected results: the activity will achieve this goal through the following four activity-level results. sub-purpose 1: improve the administrative and technical capacity of regional platforms to engage, coordinate, and manage stakeholders to collectively influence locally prioritized development. sub-purpose 2: improve the leadership skills of individual members of the regional platforms. sub-purpose 3:assist regional platforms to attract and leverage private sector support and investments. sub-purpose 4: strengthen research partnerships to inform local decision-making and development assistance.

title.narrative: Regional Health Integration to Enhance Services in Eastern Uganda Activity (RHITES-E)

description.narrative: The RHITES-E Activity helps the government of Uganda expand access to and use of high-quality health services across 30 districts and two cities. The initiative reaches some 7 million people in Eastern Uganda and Karamoja with services for HIV/AIDS; malaria; tuberculosis; maternal, newborn and child health; family planning; WASH; and nutrition. Beginning in FY22, RHITES-E transitioned direct service delivery support to the MoH at the district level, as well as strengthened several local recipients of direct USAID funding. In FY23, RHITES-E will further strengthen the governance, leadership and management capacity of 30 health districts, two regional referral hospitals and three local NGO/private Implementing Partners to increase accessibility, and utilization of quality integrated HIV, TB, and family health services. Major activities include addressing leadership and governance as well as staffing challenges at the district level. Through enhanced multi-sectoral collaboration and planning, the program engages district and sub-county stakeholders to strengthen existing community structures, reduce drivers of teenage pregnancies, and promote adequate nutrition practices, among others. RHITES-E staff advise district health management teams and district mentors to carry out data-driven support supervision to improve the maternal and child health response, and to conduct health system strengthening (HSS) targeted to enhancing the overall district family health (FH) response. RHITES-E specialists facilitate meetings to review progress on the transition to local leadership and implementation of sustainability plans to improve quality and uptake of services in poorly performing health facilities. Though IntraHealths Data to Action (D2A) methodology, RHITES-E develops the capacity of health workers through technical working groups to review FH performance, identify service quality and access gaps, and plan follow up coaching and mentorship. description.narrative: The initiative will train lay community members to provide depression screening and treatment to participants in USAID programs centered on child protection, health, education, economic growth, and human rights. description.narrative: The Civic Engagement Activity is to enhance citizen participation in social and political processes in Uganda, with a particular focus on youth. The USAID Ethiopia Civic Engagement Activity aimed to strengthen Ethiopias social fabric. By fostering a vibrant civic environment, the initiative sought to mitigate conflicts and empower marginalized groups. The USAID Ethiopia Civic Engagement (ECE) activity endeavored to overcome deep-seated citizen distrust and foster inclusive dialogue, respect for human rights, and citizen-responsive governance to strengthen Ethiopias social fabric and advance sustainable development goals. The activity supported inclusive dialogue, human rights, and effective governance through civil society organizations and community-based actors. The activity issued grants to civil society organizations, universities, institutes and others to conduct research, run training, pilot novel civic engagement ideas, run advocacy campaigns and more. ECE used the collective impact approach, which calls for multiple organizations or entities to align their individual agendas in favor of a shared common agenda, to foster multi-stakeholder civic partnerships. This approach was activated via problem-driven iterative adaptation as a core methodology to support joint action among local system actors, deconstruct complex challenges and address root issues. Through this approach, civil society networks co-created activities and built capacity for themselves and the sector. The ECE and its partners served as facilitators and supporters in fostering community, connection and trust.

title.narrative: Supporting Public Sector Workplaces to Expand Action and Responses Against HIV/AIDS (SPEAR)

description.narrative: USAIDs SPEAR program, a nationwide workplace project, enabled more than 12,200 government workers to deliver workplace-based HIV services to over 710,000 public sector employees, police and prison personnel, their families, and the surrounding communities. Services included HIV counseling and testing, sexual prevention behavior change peer education, family planning, elimination of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), antiretroviral therapy and support, and tuberculosis screening and treatment. An accelerated scale-up by training health workers resulted in circumcision of over 48,000 men, including pioneering expansion to the Karamoja region in the final year of the project. The project also supported the Uganda Police Force and the Prisons Services to receive accreditation of 19 ART service sites and 14 Option B+ service sites, resulting in 1,291 people started on Option B+ and over 8,000 on ART.

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Strengthening Tuberculosis & HIV/AIDS Response in the Eastern Region of Uganda - (STAR E)

description.narrative: Strengthening Tuberculosis (TB) and HIV/AIDS Responses in East Uganda (STAR-E) main focus is strengthening Tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS prevention, care and treatment in twelve districts of the Eastern region of Uganda (Budaka, Bududa, Bukwa, Busia, Butaleja, Kapchorwa, Mbale, Pallisa, Sironko, Bulambuli,Kween and Kibuku). STAR-E priority result areas include: 1) increased uptake of comprehensive HIV/AIDS and TB services; 2) decentralized service delivery systems strengthened for improved uptake of quality HIV/AIDS and TB services, and institutionalize national Lot Quality Assurance Sample surveys; 3) quality HIV/AIDS and TB services delivered in all supported health facilities and community organizations; 4) networks, linkages and referral systems established or strengthened with and between health facilities and communities to improve access to and uptake of comprehensive HIV/AIDS and TB services; and 5) increased demand for comprehensive HIV/AIDS and TB prevention, care and treatment services.

title.narrative: Strengthening Tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS Response in East Central Uganda (STAR-EC)

description.narrative: Strengthening Tuberculosis (TB) and HIV/AIDS Responses in East and Central Uganda (STAR-EC) is a five-year, $55 million program awarded in March 2009. Its main focus is strengthening Tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS awareness, prevention, care and treatment in six districts in East Central Uganda ( Bugiri Iganga, Kaliro Kamuli Mayuge and Namutumba). STAR-EC aims to achieving the following result areas: 1) increased uptake of comprehensive HIV/AIDS and TB services; 2) decentralized service delivery systems strengthened for improved uptake of quality HIV/AIDS and TB services; 3) quality HIV/AIDS and TB services delivered in all supported health facilities and community organizations; 4) networks, linkages, and referral systems established or strengthened with and between health facilities and communities to improve access to and uptake of comprehensive HIV/AIDS and TB services; and 5) increased demand for comprehensive HIV/AIDS and TB prevention, care and treatment services.

The USAID/CMM-funded Building Bridges to Peace (BBP) program sought to address the key causes of conflict in and around northern Karamoja by engaging communities in inter-group dialogues and joint livelihoods projects that build mutual interest and promote reconciliation. Its main objectives were to strengthen local mechanisms for conflict mitigation, support reconciliation through dialogues and trust-building measures, and build cooperation and address key causes of violence through joint livelihoods projects.

title.narrative: Securing Ugandan's Right to Essential Medicines (SURE)

description.narrative: Securing Ugandans' Right for Essential Medicines (Uganda SURE) aims to aims to assist the Government of Ugandas commitment to strengthen the national pharmaceutical supply system to ensure that the people of Uganda have access to adequate quantities of good quality essential medicines and health supplies. To achieve this goal, SURE's objectives are to: 1) Improve Uganda's policy, legal, and regulatory framework to produce pharmaceutical supply chain stability and sustainability; 2) Improve capacity and performance of central government entities to carry out their supply chain management responsibilities; 3) Improve capacity and performance of districts, health subdistricts, and implementing partners in their supply chain management roles. SURE works on integrating Uganda's supply chain and establishing a pharmaceutical management information system that provides full transparency to minimize medicine stock-outs and waste.

(Uganda): .This mechanism focuses on critical health systems interventions for quality service delivery. In FY 2016, the scope includes: continued district government capacity building to lead, plan, monitor, and implement family planning/reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child health (FP/RMNCH), nutrition and HIV interventions; support to civil society to demand accountability for results; provide performance based grants to improve FP/MNCH services; support health financing initiatives at district and national level including national health insurance, program based budgeting, domestic resource mobilization, while addressing issues of efficiency in the health sector; strengthen and harmonize community systems, including support for the development and roll-out of community health extension workers strategy. Also, it supports human resources for health by seconding critical cadre for MNCH services in districts where gaps and heavy burden exist........

title.narrative: Long Term Family Planning Methods Program (LTM)

description.narrative: (Uganda): LTM's objective is to increase access to long term and permanent FP in Uganda. With $316,000 in FY 2014 the LTM activity will: 1) Expand to include other reproductive health services (two new outreach teams will be added to the existing 24 teams in areas with high unmet need and high client demand). The teams will provide 12,663 FP services, leading to 15,183 Couple Years of Protection; 2) Integrate HIV testing and cervical cancer screening in 16 districts. 15,120 integrated services will be provided; 3) Strengthen the national health system by embedding 75 dedicated providers (DPs) at hospital-level public or Private Not-For-Profit (PNFP) health facilities. The DPs will serve a cluster of 3 surrounding Health Center IVs and IIIs in the public and PNFP sectors. These FP champions will provide services and improve the ability of host facilities to sustainably provide services - mentoring, improving stock management, integrating FP into activities, and engaging district leadership.

title.narrative: Strengthening Tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS response in the Southwestern region of Uganda (STAR-SW)

description.narrative: The STAR-SW project works to increase utilization of, access to, and coverage of quality comprehensive HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis (TB) services in 184 health facilities in the 13 districts in South Western Uganda. EGPAF aims to integrate cost-effective, family-based HIV/AIDS care and treatment services and prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (PMTCT) programs into health care facilities through a multidisciplinary program of training, infrastructure development, and technical support. To enhance the sustainability of services, EGPAF promotes local district ownership of all activities; all work planning and roll-out of new services are led by the District Ministry of Health, and mentoring and supervising includes the District Health Team as the provider of support.

The Targeted HIV/AIDS and Laboratory Services (THALAS) project will provide specialized laboratory services and advanced care and treatment in seven sites including Kampala. The project will work collaboratively with the Ministry of Health and the Strengthening Uganda's Systems for Treating AIDS Nationally (SUSTAIN) project to build the capacity of lab personnel in regional and district hospitals in the provision of high-quality lab services.

title.narrative: Sustainable Responses for Improving the Lives of Vulnerable Children and th

description.narrative: Sustainable Responses for Improving the Lives of Vulnerable Children and their Households: The program will focus on improving household economic and food security, enhancing protection and legal services for vulnerable children and empowering and strengthening families with the ability to access, acquire or provide critical services for women and children such as health, education and psychosocial support.

title.narrative: An Entrepreneurial Model of Community Health Delivery in Uganda

description.narrative: Despite a substantial decline in child mortality in recent years, millions of children still die from preventable diseases every year. In this study in rural Uganda, researchers evaluate the impact of a micro-franchise model, which incentivizes door-to-door health workers, on under-five mortality rates.

(Uganda): SHRP will continue to build government and other stakeholder.capacity to support classroom and community behavior change to improve early.grade reading (EGR) and HIV knowledge, attitudes, and practices. SHRP works through.established Government of Uganda (GOU) systems to improve capacity to.effectively teach reading in early grades through professional development and.support activities for college tutors, teachers, and head teachers. SHRP will.directly reach an estimated 2.3 million pupils in 3,702 schools and provide.technical support to the GOU to scale up the EGR intervention to an.additional 1.2 million children.in 2,644 primary schools..In combination with a third USAID-funded activity, more than 90% of Uganda's.pupils will be benefit from the EGR program. SHRP's basic education.components are complemented by PEPFAR-funded activities that provide HIV and.health education programming to 34,000 upper primary and secondary school.pupils.
