(Uganda): .This activity strengthens the capacity of a local company to become a sustainable manufacturer and distributor of therapeutic and supplementary foods. It addresses the needs of severely/moderately malnourished individuals with a particular focus on children, women and people living with HIV/AIDS. This activity improves the farmer livelihoods by providing support to small-scale rural farmers to produce raw materials for the production of the foods. FY 2016 funds will be used to support farmer groups to produce quality raw materials, purchase and distribute therapeutic and supplementary foods, and strengthen local capacity for logistics management. These activities lead to improved agricultural production and economic livelihoods among small scale farmers and a strong distribution system for the therapeutic and supplementary foods resulting in improved nutrition status..

title.narrative: Northern Uganda Health Integration to Enhance Services - (NUHITES

description.narrative: (Uganda): NUHITES implements an integrated health program in 15 districts in northern Uganda at facility and community levels. This activity will be supported by $6,184,000 in Global Health Program ($800,000 in TB, $1,084,000 in Malaria, $2,700,000 in MCH, $1,000,000 in Family Planning and Reproductive Health and $600,000 in Nutrition), as well as PEPFAR funds. The project goal is improved and sustained health and nutrition status of the northern Uganda population through: district-based system strengthening and integrated services for HIV/AIDS; TB; malaria; maternal, newborn and child health; reproductive health and family planning; and nutrition. The expected outcome for the NUHITES project at the end of the five years is to contribute to the reduction of health mortality and morbidity and further prevent occurrences of infectious diseases in the target area.

title.narrative: Tourism for Biodiversity and Economic Growth

description.narrative: The activity aims to use eco-tourism to reduce threats to biodiversity. The program will help develop Uganda's nature-based tourism industry to deliver an improved experience for visitors and improved stewardship of the natural resources necessary to sustain Uganda's economic development.

title.narrative: Good Life Integrated HIV Counseling and Testing Kampala project

description.narrative: Project Goal: To contribute to the prevention of further HIV transmission and improvement of the quality of life of individuals infected through early diagnosis and linkages to prevention, care and treatment. Overall objective of the project: To increase access to coverage of, and utilization of quality, comprehensive HIV/TB prevention, care, and treatment services for communities within the 5 divisions of Kampala. The project will be delivered through 4 key result areas, that address the specific objectives as below; 1. To increase demand for HCT services as an entry point to prevention and care services. 2. To increase access to and utilization of HCT services among most at risk populations. 3. To strengthen networks, referral systems and linkages to other HIV/AIDS, TB, Reproductive Health, Maternal and Child Health services. 4. To build capacity for sustainability of services initiated by the project.

Akimorikin (coming together) activity, a conflict mitigation and management activity in the Karamoja region. Akimorikin will strengthen institutional capacity for effective Early Warning and Early Response in Karamoja. IRCs peace building program incorporates a strong gender dimension, contributing to the UNSCRs 1325 & 1820, and the Government of Uganda National Action Plan in support of these resolutions. The program objectives are achieved through strong partnerships with local Civil Society Organizations, government institutions and IGADs CEWERU in Uganda. IRCs peace building work covers the districts of Amudat, Nakapiripirit, Moroto, Napak and Kotido.

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Communication for Healthy Communities (CHC) activity provides strategic social and behavior change communication (SBCC) support across USAID/Uganda's health and HIV portfolios. With FY 2018 funds, the activity will support Government of Uganda (GOU) and USG implementing partners to design and implement high quality SBCC interventions to increase the use of family planning (FP), including long-acting and reversible contraceptive methods targeting youth and women; improve nutrition behaviors and practices, especially in the first 1,000 days after an infant's birth; increase recognition of danger signs during pregnancy; improve uptake of antenatal care within the first 16 weeks of pregnancy; improve early and prompt health-seeking behavior at facilities for maternal, newborn, and childhood illnesses; increase prompt treatment of malaria in children; improve malaria prevention behaviors including the use of insecticide treated nets; increase tuberculosis treatment completion; and strengthen risk communication for the mitigation, preparation, and response to emerging pandemic threats and infectious disease outbreaks in Uganda... .

title.narrative: Northern Uganda Development of Enhanced Local Governance, Infrastructure, and Livelihoods (NUDEIL) Support Services

description.narrative: Under this 18-month project, ACTED will support the overall objectives of the Northern Uganda Development of Enhanced Local Governance, Infrastructure, and Livelihoods (NUDEIL) program, a small-scale government-to-government pilot infrastructure-rehabilitation program. ACTED will provide direct support to assist the District Local Governments to achieve their NUDEIL Operational Plans (NOP) and quality assurance oversight. This will lead to the construction or rehabilitation of more than 270 kilometres of road, 22.5 kilometres of road structures, 81 building structures and 252 water points.

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Uganda Value-Added Maize Alliance is a public-private partnership Global Development Alliance with a local maize-processing firm (and other resource partners) for a three-year activity valued at $9.8 million; the partners will contribute $7.2 million and the Mission will leverage this with $2.6 million in USAID funds. The alliance intends to increase the capacity of farmers to produce high-quality maize and aggregate this production so that the private sector will have a reliable supply of inputs for maize processing. The 9,500 participating smallholder farmer households will receive a 30% price premium paid for higher quality maize and experience a 50% reduction in current post-harvest losses at the village level, and the partners will invest in processing equipment and facilities to produce maize bran and germ, as well as corn syrup; all products that have a viable market in Uganda up the value chain to food processers and beverage producers who will realize significant cost-savings from locally produced syrup, bran and germ.

(Uganda): .The Alur Highlands Coffee Alliance activity is a public-private partnership between USAID and Ecom Agroindustrial Corporation Ltd, a global commodity-trading firm that specializes in coffee and other agricultural products. The alliance, which is implemented by the CARANA Corporation, is a three-year activity valued at $7.5 million. Ecom will contribute nearly $3.5 million in investment through its local subsidiary, Kawacom, and USAID will leverage this involvement with an additional $3.9 million in funds. This catalytic partnership should increase the saleable yields and quality of high-value Arabica coffee produced by previously unreachable farmers in the West Nile region by: providing them training on good agricultural practices and access to finance, constructing post-harvest processing facilities, applying geo-traceablity to their farms and certifying their coffee as sustainably produced, and providing a link to the global specialty-coffee market...

title.narrative: Education and Research to Improve Climate Change Adaptation activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): .Focused GCC- Adaptation funding of $565,308 will be used to enhance resilience and reduce vulnerability to climate change of people, places and livelihoods upon which they depend by informing the Government of Uganda's plans, strategies and policies. This activity partners with Makerere University's Centre for Climate Change Research and Innovation (MUCCRI) to improve the level of education, professional expertise, and research to help meet the challenge of adapting to climate variability and change in the agricultural sector. The Activity will: (1) help transform MUCCRI into a leading center for climate change education and research in Africa; (2) develop capacity of university staff, government officials, civil society, and the private sector; (3) improve all levels of university education in climate science, meteorology, and climate adaptation; and (4) conduct and disseminate climate change impacts, and adaptation research. ...

Develop and conduct needs assessments, baseline studies, targeted evaluations, special studies or other information-gathering efforts specifically for the design, monitoring and evaluation of USG-funded programs. This sub-element may also include developing and disseminating best practices and lessons learned, testing demonstration and/or pilot models, or the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks. Note: All such activities that are carried out by partners as an integral part of their monitoring and evaluation efforts for programs funded under other sub-elements should be included within those sub-elements.

(Uganda): .Advocacy for Better Health will support advocacy efforts, targeting a range of Family Planning, MCH, Nutrition and WASH and HIV issues in 35 districts with funds from Global Health Program and PEPFAR accounts. In FY 2018, the activity will support local civil society engagement to: 1) increase citizens' demand for quality services; 2) hold government accountable for its commitment to transparency, and accountability in service delivery; 3) decrease stigma and discrimination; and 4) promote sustainability of efforts for improved the quality and availability of essential health, and HIV services. By strengthening citizens' voices through civil society organizations, the activity will promote country ownership of social sector reforms, accountability, rights based services and drive country ownership at all levels to sustain community feedback, improve quality of services and utilization of data to inform programming. .. .. .

(Uganda): The Rights and Rule of Law (RROL) activity implemented by Freedom House supports judicial independence, effective civil society, human rights advocacy, and media freedom in Uganda. As the space for civil society and the media to operate especially in the areas of freedom of assembly and expression is expected to continue shrinking, the role of the judiciary, civil society and media will be critical in addressing rights and rule of law issues in Uganda. With FY 2017 funds, the activity will support that role through human rights training of women judges, judicial officials and journalists. It will support continuous professional development opportunities for judges and magistrates, civil society and media actors and also support strategic litigation to uphold human rights. RROL will also continue to work with Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Intersex organizations that work with state institutions, and other non-state actors in the promotion of human rights.

description.narrative: (Uganda): UHSC aims to increase the availability, accessibility and appropriate use of essential medicines and health supplies (EMHS) through reform of national policies and strategies to maximize efficiency, transparency and equity in use of EMHS resources and country capacity building for effective management of supply chain operations. Expected results in FY2015 include: advocating for revision in health care budget allocation; continuation of action on improving access to life-saving medicines for women and children; expansion of performance assessment, supervision and reporting system nationally; introduction/implementation integrated logistics management information system for improved data availability at all levels; and continued progress in integrating health commodity management in pre-service curricula.

description.narrative: Sustain the productivity of the agricultural sector through investments that foster increasing returns to land, labor, and capital. Targeted interventions to male and female producers provide improvements in technology and management practices, expanded access to markets and credit, increased organizational and market efficiency, and restoration and protection of resiliency in production and livelihood systems.

(Uganda): .The HIV/Health Initiatives in Workplaces Activity (HIWA) aims to improve the health of employees of the Uganda Police Force (UPF), 11 Private Security Companies (PSC), Uganda's seven conservation areas under the Uganda Wildlife Authority (UWA) and 80 select hotels under the Uganda Hotel Owners Association (UHOA). Working in 54 districts across Uganda, HIWA reaches not only the target population of 111,624 employees of the selected occupational sectors, but also their family members and communities. With FY 2018 funds, HIWA will increase access to and uptake and use of quality maternal and child health, family planning, TB, nutrition, HIV/AIDS and WASH services. To reach this goal, HIWA will: strengthen provision of advanced quality and respectful reproductive, maternal, neonatal and child health (RMNCH) care in communities and at health facilities; create demand, increase access, and improve uptake of quality RMNCH services; increase access to rights-based, quality family planning services for all women, especially youth and low parity women; strengthen integration of the Nutrition, Assessment, Counseling and Support (NACS) interventions in the Feed the Future zone of influence by building health worker capacity and scaling-up high impact interventions; promote WASH services through adoption of "small doable actions" at health facilities and in communities to reduce morbidity in under five children; and scale-up gender based violence prevention and treatment... .

title.narrative: Better Outcomes for Children in the Northern & Eastern Uganda

description.narrative: The purpose of this activity is to enable more OVC, youth and their caregivers in Uganda, and particularly in Eastern and Northern Regions, to access core services for improving health, nutrition, food security, education, and psychosocial well-being and to prevent and respond to child abuse, exploitation and neglect.

title.narrative: Sustainable Outcomes for Children and Youth (SOCY)

description.narrative: Sustainable Outcomes for Children and Youth in Central and Western Uganda is implementing a household-based response to empower vulnerable children, youths and their caregivers to reduce their vulnerability and improve their wellbeing. The project is implemented in the Southwestern districts of Bushenyi, Rukungiri, Kiruhura, Kabale and Isingiro. The project targets to reach a total of 150453 direct beneficiaries (including vulnerable children and their caregivers) from 24654 households in a period of 3 years. The program activities involving at least 2268 Community volunteers (i.e. Para-social workers, VHTs and Para-legal workers) is implemented at sub-county level covering a total of 83 sub-counties. The project goal is to create an integrated and coordinated service delivery system that will ensure access to essential health, nutrition and social services by OVC, youth and their caregivers resulting in better outcomes and reduced HIV/AIDS vulnerability in the target districts.

title.narrative: Long Term Family Planning Bridge Activity (LTFP)

description.narrative: (Uganda): This is a bridge activity using $9M from USAID and $11M from DFID between the Expanding Access to Long Term and Permanent Methods (LAPM) for Family Planning (FP) Program and its follow-on. It will increase the breadth and depth of FP service delivery in Uganda through 1) expanding geographic coverage and reach of FP services; 2) increasing affordability, particularly the provision of LAPM; 3) strengthening the capacity of the public sector to deliver LAPM; and 4) integrating reproductive health services with HIV testing, STI treatment, and cervical cancer screening (CCS). In FY2015, LTFP will use mobile outreach teams to provide FP services in 111 districts, and integrate HIV testing and CCS in 16 districts. It will also strengthen local health systems by embedding 75 dedicated providers at hospital-level public or Private Not-For-Profit health facilities to sustainably provide services - mentoring, improving stock management, integrating FP, and engaging district leadership. This activity will also include demand creation activities and SBCC to address barriers to the uptake of FP services. This activity will also include demand creation activities and SBCC activities using channels such as the print and electronic media, person-to-person communications, communications group discussions, and mobile technology to address barriers to the uptake of FP services in all districts of Uganda.

(Uganda): The Literacy Achievement and Retention Activity (LARA) will continue to support the Government of Uganda's national early grade reading (EGR) program by transforming reading instruction and reducing gender-based violence in order to increase retention and improve learning outcomes in primary schools. LARA's interventions will reach an estimated 1.4 million pupils in 3,200 schools. LARA prints and distributes textbooks and teacher guides in English and three local languages; delivers targeted teacher training; provides post-training support, supervision, and monitoring; and conducts EGR assessments. LARA increases retention by identifying and training local change agents who in turn provide training and support to teachers, community members, and pupils to prevent bullying, corporal punishment and sexual abuse. In addition, referral networks are established and local child protection services strengthened to both respond to and prevent violence against children.

title.narrative: Regional Health Integration to Enhance Services in South West Uganda (RHITES SW)

description.narrative: (Uganda): RHITES-SW supports 18 districts, with approximately 4.6 million people. While portions of the HIV and TB portfolio have already transitioned to local partners, in its last year, RHITES-SW will support completing the integrated high-quality maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH); family planning (FP); tuberculosis (TB); nutrition; and water, hygiene, and sanitation (WASH) interventions in these districts. With $ 400,000 in FY 2021 funds, four areas will be prioritized: consolidating the high-impact, evidence-based interventions; strengthening community-level interventions to increase demand and uptake of quality health services; health system strengthening to improve health services; and strengthening health information systems including data collection, completeness, and utilization. .To ensure continuation of services in the current COVID-19 pandemic, RHITES-SW will align its interventions and responses, including COVID-19 vaccine rollout, based on the Ugandan Ministry of Health guidelines. This will include targeted provision of personal protective equipment for service providers and beneficiaries of MNCH, FP, TB, and nutrition services..RHITES-SW will engage with all stakeholders and beneficiaries to identify, plan, and implement local solutions to health challenges. RHITES-SW will promote commitment and capacity to provide high-quality health services..

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Social Marketing Activity will serve as USAID Uganda's flagship program for Social Marketing and successor to USAID Uganda's AFFORD program, which ended in September 2014. The program's goal is to contribute to a reduction in new HIV infections, total fertility, maternal and child mortality, malnutrition and malaria, and to improve access to family planning.This four-year activity aims to improve utilization of health-related social marketing products and services among under-served Ugandan consumers in rural and urban areas. With FY 2015 GHP funds, this activity will increase the demand for and utilization of family planning, nutrition, malaria, and maternal and child health services to a number of target audiences, including those in hard-to-reach areas. This activity will also strengthen systems for local organizations to ensure sustained, equitable access to health products and services.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Producer Organizations Activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): .The overall objective of the Feed the Future Producer Organizations (PO) activity is to strengthen the governance, management, service delivery and local-level advocacy capacities of producer organizations. The activity supports secondary POs to be critical change leaders in equipping member POs with the skills, knowledge and linkages needed to mature and develop into sustainable businesses that meet the demands of their membership. The goal is to help establish durable and enduring institutions that are able to plan, mobilize resources, and deliver services that meet the evolving needs of their members. The expected results include: (1) Increased involvement of POs in business-oriented activities along the values chains; and (2) Improved PO governance and management structures that efficiently provide services to the members...

(Uganda): .The Fertilizer Innovation Alliance program aims to improve farmers' yields and income per unit area through better access to soil testing services and affordable blended fertilizer. The program works with Akorion, a youth-led Information and Communication Technology company and the Ugandan National Agrodealers Association (UNADA) to improve farmers' access to affordable, customized site-specific fertilizers and soil-testing services that will improve adoption of fertilizers in Uganda and crop productivity. The alliance will build a modern fertilizer blending facility to market appropriately sized fertilizer packages to farmers; promote improved fertilized uptake through demonstration plots; build capacity of middle actors to commercialize blended fertilizers; and build a sustainable network of distributors...

title.narrative: Regional Health Integration to Enhance Services in East Central Uganda (RHITES-EC)

description.narrative: (Uganda): RHITES-EC supports implementation of integrated maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH), family planning (FP), malaria, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis (TB), nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation (WASH) interventions in 12 districts serving a population of approximately four million people. With $6,008,591 million in FY 2020 funds, four areas will be prioritized: scaling up and advancing quality high-impact interventions; strengthening community-level interventions to increase uptake of services; strengthening health systems to improve the delivery of services, and strengthening data systems, data quality, and utilization. Major activities include: strengthening district coordination and management of health investments and outcomes pertaining to service delivery, increasing coverage through integrated community outreach, and strengthening supply chain management..To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, RHITES-EC will align interventions with Ugandan Ministry of Health guidance. This will integrate infection prevention and control activities and support targeted provision of personal protective equipment to protect service providers and beneficiaries of MNCH, FP, TB, and nutrition services. .RHITES-EC will support communities to identify and address structural, social, and patient-related barriers to seeking health care. The activity will support district coordination mechanisms and stakeholder platforms to enhance resource allocation and advocacy to improve MNCH and FP services. .RHITES-EC will contribute to the Mission's Journey to Self-Reliance vision through meaningful engagements with all stakeholders and beneficiaries to identify, plan, and implement local solutions to health challenges, promoting commitment, and capacity to provide quality health services...

Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Regional Health Integration to Enhance Services in Eastern Region (RHITES-E)

description.narrative: (Uganda): The activity supports maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH), family planning (FP), HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis (TB), nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation (WASH) interventions in 30 districts covering a population of approximately six million people. With $6,143,2705 in FY 2020 funds, it will prioritize scaling up and strengthening: implementation of high-impact, evidence-based interventions; community-level interventions to increase demand and uptake of health services; strengthening health systems to improve health services, and improving the data collection and use of health information systems..Major activities include: capacity-building to improve knowledge, skills, and competence; mentorship; promoting evidence-based decision-making and using data to prioritize interventions; and strengthening supply chain management for effective use of commodities. It will implement a quality improvement approach to address gaps in service delivery, undertake infrastructure improvements for MNCH services, and address underlying behavioral, cultural, and environmental constraints to improve WASH. It will increase access to age appropriate FP information and services, and improve community-level TB case finding and treatment success rates.To ensure continuation of services during the COVID-19 pandemic, RHITES-E will align interventions with Ugandan Ministry of Health guidance. This will integrate infection prevention and control activities and support targeted provision of personal protective equipment for service providers and beneficiaries of MNCH, FP, TB, and nutrition services..It will engage stakeholders and utilize community platforms to support better health seeking behaviors. RHITES-E will contribute to the Journey to Self-Reliance vision through meaningful engagement of stakeholders and beneficiaries to identify, plan, and implement local solutions to health challenges, promoting commitment and capacity to provide quality health services..

description.narrative: (Uganda): With $1,850,000 in FY 2021 funds, Defeat TB will provide technical assistance to the National TB program, USAID implementing partners, and focus districts to reduce Uganda's TB burden and contribute to the U.S. Government and World Health Organization's End TB Strategy, which seeks to end the global TB epidemic by 2035. The activity works directly with the Ministry of Health leadership to address the high TB burden in Uganda and focuses on finding missing TB cases through effective community and facility-based interventions. .The activity will partner with other U.S. Government-supported TB and HIV partners. This coordination includes: providing support to the National TB Leprosy program to improve the quality of the current Multi Drug-Resistant-TB program, developing and implementing strategies that mitigate impact of COVID-19, increasing screening and detection of all forms of TB, improving early treatment initiation and successful treatment completion, and strengthening community systems to support the continuum of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. .

(Uganda): USAID supports the Uganda National Malaria Control Strategic Plan goals for indoor residual spraying (IRS), aiming to cover 85 percent of all structures and protect at least 85 percent of the population in 14 target districts in Northern Uganda. In FY 2015, this program will conduct two rounds of spraying in the target districts. Approximately 1,100,000 houses will be sprayed and more than three million people will be protected. Other activities to be implemented by the program include IRS capacity building for national and district vector control teams, support to the Gulu insectary, entomological and environmental monitoring, and behavior change and community mobilization activities. The President's Malaria Initiative will continue with capacity development of the public and private sector (i.e. the Ministry of Health, district local governments, and private companies) to provide appropriate supervision and oversight of IRS activities.

title.narrative: Supporting Access to Justice, Fostering Peace and Equity (SAFE)

description.narrative: (Uganda): .SAFE supports peaceful resolution of conflict arising from land disputes, oil exploration and ethnic diversity, and the residual effects of the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) conflict in northern Uganda, as a basis for economic growth and service delivery. Working at the national and subnational level, SAFE promotes peaceful resolution of land disputes by promoting dialogue between the Government of Uganda's land management and administration institutions, civil society organizations (CSOs) and other stakeholders. It promotes post conflict reconciliation and psychosocial wellbeing among conflict- affected communities. The activity will also build the capacity of CSOs and private sector groups to enhance the development of agriculture and investment in Uganda...

title.narrative: Performance and Impact Evaluation of Literacy and Health Education Program

description.narrative: (Uganda): The LARA P&IE service contract will provide technical assistance to conduct a performance and impact evaluation of the five-year Literacy Achievement and Retention Activity (LARA) in Uganda (RFA 617-15-00009). One major purpose of this performance and impact evaluation is to explore the extent to which intended outcomes are being achieved, and the effectiveness of different program approaches and interventions. The impact evaluation will test the extent to which the program's activities improve reading skills and retention in primary grades. A particular focus will be the activity's interventions that address student safety and school-related gender-based violence (SRGBV), and to what extent these interventions result in measurable impact on student learning, specifically early grade reading.

title.narrative: Feed the Future (FTF) Agricultural Inputs Activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): The Agricultural Inputs Activity will increase the responsible use of high-quality agriculture inputs through improving private sector supply chain management, decreasing the prevalence of counterfeit products, and raising awareness of the benefits of quality inputs use through advanced marketing and sales techniques in rural Uganda. Activities include: (1) strengthening relationships between actors in the inputs supply chain; (2) assisting suppliers and retailers with inventory management; (3) marketing, and sales force promotion; (4) increasing the use of verified products and tamper proof packaging; (5) improving the technical capacity of input retailers; (6) improving the capacity of domestic inputs industry associations, and (7) scaling up production and dissemination of improved varieties of maize and beans. The activity will also support climate change adaptation through dissemination of improved agronomic practices and technologies that will help farmers build resilience to the adverse effects of climate change.

(Uganda): The Governance, Accountability, Participation, and Performance (GAPP) activity is jointly funded by USAID and UKAID. It aims at improving local governance, strengthening national accountability institutions and supporting citizen participation. By fostering engagement between district officials, national-level decision makers and citizens, it supports improved accountability, participation and performance. FY 2017 funds will support civil society and private sector to involve youth in advocacy for public policy and service delivery in health and agriculture. Funds will also support a parliamentary forum to rally Members of Parliament around improving health service delivery with attention to the shrinking health budget allocations and public health care services. Working with entities such as women-owned and youth agri-businesses, it will help improve agriculture extension services through effective engagement of private sector in local governance processes.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Commodity Production and Marketing activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): The objective of the activity is to improve competitiveness of the coffee, maize, and bean value chains by achieving sustainable increases in the production and marketing of high-quality maize, beans, and coffee in 34 Feed the Future focus districts. The expected results include: increased crop productivity; increased availability and effectiveness of support services; strengthened inter-actor relationships for better movement of products and information between buyers and sellers; and increased access to competitive markets. ...

title.narrative: Feed the Future Enabling Environment for Agriculture activity

description.narrative: (Uganda): This activity partners with private and public sector institutions to improve the enabling environment for agricultural development, trade with American small businesses and national security interests. It is an integral part of the Feed the Future initiative, and contributes to achieving sustainable increases in agriculture sector incomes and trade. It aims to: 1) remove policy and regulatory constraints to increase trade capacity for American and local companies, agricultural production, processing, and marketing of goods; 2) strengthen capacity of Government of Uganda (GOU) institutions to facilitate agricultural development and trade, which addresses concerns of marginalized populations susceptible to social unrest; 3) strengthen capacity of GOU institutions to respond to adverse weather impacts on agriculture; and 4) enhance capacity of Ugandan private sector and civil society institutions to contribute to policy decisions related to agricultural development, and trade.

(Uganda): .This activity mobilizes the private sector to provide high-quality health services from private-for-profit and private not-for-profit providers. It collaborates across all sectors to expand availability of services by private providers; increase affordability of services; and improve private health facilities and services across a range of RMNCH, nutrition and HIV services. It provides technical assistance to the private sector to build structures to regulate and monitor quality and compliance according to standards, report to the national HMIS, network and coordination. It engages in discussions around national health policy, resource allocation and programming for sustained delivery of quality services, and supports the professional medical councils, the Ministry of Health, Public-Private Partnership for Health, and district coordinating committees to provide expertise, enhance quality standards, improve access to credit, support accreditation and provide leadership......

description.narrative: (Uganda): MELP will continue to strengthen USAID/Uganda's monitoring and evaluation (M&E) function; improve USAID's organizational practices and capacity for learning and adaptation; and strengthen coordination, collaboration and synergy within the Mission and with other key stakeholders. In FY 2015, MELP will continue to provide technical assistance, mentoring, training and capacity building to Mission and implementing partner staff to strengthen systems and practices in M&E, learning, and adaptation. MELP will also continue to work to strengthen the Health Management Information System (HMIS) at national and sub-national levels. It will also facilitate the development of professional relationships and network-building with relevant to create meaningful relationships and coalitions around particular bodies of specialized development knowledge to enhance both USAID and the GOU's development interventions.

title.narrative: Environmental Management for the Oil Sector

description.narrative: (Uganda): .The Environmental Management for the Oil Sector activity partners with Makerere University, Government of Uganda (GOU) environmental management institutions, local government and civil society to improve their capacity to manage oil and gas industry impacts on Uganda's biodiversity, by achieving the following expected results: (1) strengthened capacity of the GOU institutions to manage environmental impacts of the oil and gas sector;(2) strengthened capacity of Ugandan professionals in the public and private sector to manage and respond to environmental impacts of the oil and gas sector; and (3) strengthened capacity of Ugandan civil society to participate in decision-making in the oil and gas sector....
USAID/Uganda Conservation Trust Fund

(Uganda): .The Youth Leadership for Agriculture activity increases economic opportunities for Ugandan female and male youth, ages 10 to 35, in agriculture-related fields to increase incomes and build entrepreneurship, leadership and workforce readiness. The activity aims to: 1) increase incomes of youth working in agricultural value chains and 2) improve skills development through formal and non-formal education and training organizations. The activity also seeks to increase the provision of quality technical, workforce readiness and entrepreneurial skills; increase opportunities for youth to demonstrate leadership and community engagement; and improve the provision of life skills for healthy living (including family planning and reproductive health information). By assisting the private sector to engage youth in new employment opportunities, the activity directly contributes to decreasing truancy and delinquency among Uganda's youth, and supports the broader stability of the country and region. .The activity also seeks to increase the provision of quality technical, workforce readiness and entrepreneurial skills; increase opportunities for youth to demonstrate leadership and community engagement; and improve the provision of life skills for healthy living (including family planning (FP) and reproductive health information). The mechanism receives $250,000 in FY 2018 FP funds, to message and link the young people to family planning services in order to delay first pregnancy among adolescents, and encourage birth-spacing to improve households' economic engagement and empowerment. The activity will closely work with Communication for Healthy Communities, the RHITES activities a district-level, health facilities and communities to enhance FP messaging and increase access to services for young people in targeted geographic areas. .. .. .

(Uganda): The objective of MAPD is to strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Health's National Malaria Control Division and District Health Management Teams, by implementing a package of high-impact malaria interventions that focus on community prevention. These interventions include the use of long lasting insecticide treated bed nets, prevention of malaria during pregnancy, strengthening of diagnostics and treatment of malaria, strengthening surveillance, and reporting. These interventions aim to decrease malaria morbidity and mortality in 52 (central, midwest, and west-Nile) target districts.The activity protects approximately 13 million people from the effects of malaria and will receive an allocation of $4,265,189 in FY 2020 funds. ...

description.narrative: (Uganda): SITES is the strategic information mechanism for the Mission's health portfolio. The activity aims to strengthen Uganda's health information systems and build Uganda's capacity to collect, analyze, disseminate, and use data for decision making at national and regional levels. With FY 2022 funds, the activity will consolidate the support to the Ministry of Health (MOH) and implementing partners to increase the quality, availability, and timeliness of tuberculosis data. With Malaria, MCH, FP and Nutrition funds, SITES will consolidate the support to the MOH Division of Health Information, the National Malaria Control Program, the Reproductive Health Division, the Child Health Division, and the Community Health Department to strengthen the quality, availability, and timeliness of reproductive health; nutrition; child health; and water, sanitation, and hygiene data at the national and subnational levels. SITES will fund activities to improve gender equality and empower women to access and use high quality health services, activities that prevent gender-based violence and address the impact of gender-based violence, multisectoral activities to improve nutrition outcomes, activities to improve access and utilization of micronutrients. By strengthening resilient health systems at national and sub-national level, the activity will respond to climate related service delivery disruptions...

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Agricultural Biotechnology Support Program II - (ABSPII) New

description.narrative: (Uganda): This vital applied-research activity is aimed at promoting the judicious use of modern biotechnology to strengthen the scientific capacity of the Uganda National Agricultural Research Organization (NARO), and to develop East African Highland Banana varieties resistant to major diseases and pests. FY 2014 funds will be used to foster progress along the transgenic crop development cycle. Specific activities include: (1) transgenic transformation of host plants; (2) greenhouse testing of transformed plants (12 lines across the different diseases and pests) and confined field testing; (3) dissemination of non-transgenic varieties that have been proven to have significant resistance to these stresses (at least 500 test plots with four hybrid varieties); and (4) training on banana transformation, molecular analysis, and execution of field tests.

title.narrative: Strengthening Human Resources for Health (SHRH) - Capacity follow on

description.narrative: (Uganda): Strengthening Human Resources for Health (SHRH) is an award under the Capacity Plus Leader with Associate mechanism. It develops the capacities of the Government of Uganda's (GOU) central Ministries, districts, and professional councils to effectively and efficiently manage their human resources for health. Expected results in FY 2018 include: National HRH strategy updated, Community Health Extension Worker training rolled out, USG-supported staff transitioned to GOU payroll, mechanisms to reduce absenteeism fully rolled out, staffing norms at regional referral hospitals and lower-level facilities revised, and recruitment projection plan for Ministry of Health (MOH) updated. Interventions will include policy implementation, review of staffing norms and revision of schemes for health workers' services, technical assistance to MOH in strategic planning, recruitment, and performance management to contribute to overall improvement and sustainability in quality of service delivery and planning... ...

(Uganda): .The Uganda Biodiversity fund supports sustainable financing for biodiversity conservation in Uganda. The activity will invite private sector actors to engage in conservation and strengthen public institutions and local organizations to manage natural resources, including biodiversity, effectively. In 2018, USAID/Uganda initiated a modification of the existing USAID/Uganda Biodiversity Trust Fund (UBTF) award to include provisions that would enable a transition award to the Uganda Biodiversity Fund (UBF), the conservation trust fund created under the UBTF Activity. Following completion of the UBTF Activity, USAID/Uganda will initiate the UBF transition award using FY 2018 funds. The goal of this award is to support Ugandan-led development by enhancing the UBF's role as a catalyst for private conservation financing and an apex partner for local conservation organizations through the mobilization of small grants. These grants will be aimed at stimulating grassroots conservation efforts in Uganda's key biodiversity areas and will demonstrate UBF's effectiveness to potential private sector donors, which will support UBF's transition to a self-sustaining entity. The prime awardee of the existing UBTF activity, the Wildlife Conservation Society, will remain engaged on the transition award as a sub-awardee to provide technical guidance..... .

description.narrative: (Uganda): USAID will complement the new SIDA/World Bank RH voucher program to increase access among poor women to skilled care during pregnancy, delivery and postpartum. The project will support: pregnant women to deliver under skilled attendance; pregnant women to attend at least 4 antenatal care (ANC) visits; women with HIV to receive PMTCT; and mothers to access post-natal care. The project focuses on safe delivery, capacity building and project management. The safe delivery component provides subsidized vouchers to poor pregnant women to access a package of safe delivery services from contracted service providers. The package will also include preventing mother-to-child transmission and malaria prevention services as part of ANC. The component on capacity building and project management will support project management functions and build national capacity to mainstream and scale-up implementation of the voucher scheme in the health sector.

Promote governance institutions, processes, and policies that are transparent and accountable across all development sectors. Support non-governmental as well as governmental institutions (including enforcement and investigation entities, independent audit agencies, anti-corruption commissions, procurement agencies, legislatures, line ministries, independent agencies, political parties, judicial actors, as well as civil society organizations, academia, press and the private sector). Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). The Karamoja Resilience Support Unit is a new activity designed to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of development assistance in the Karamoja region through targeted support to improve coordination across projects, activities, and agencies active in Karamoja. The goal is to foster mutual learning, knowledge management, and coordination among the stakeholders, leading to a supportive policy environment and increased impacts of programming on drought resilience and growth. Objectives: 1. facilitate implementation of the Building Resilience to Recurrent Crisis, 2. provide a range of strategic, programmatic and logistical support to the Karamoja Development Partner Group (KDPG), 3. provide targeted support to strengthen Government of Uganda policies and systems that build resilience in Karamoja, 4. provide analytic support and an evidence base for Objectives 1-3 via rapid appraisals, studies, evaluations and other applied practical research exercises.

title.narrative: Livelihoods and Enterprises for Agricultural development (LEAD).

description.narrative: LEAD was initially designed to catalyze the transformation of Ugandas agricultural economy by facilitating competitiveness in select agricultural value chains. Following a successful mid-term evaluation, LEAD focused activities on the three FtF value chainsmaize, beans, and coffeeand modified its approach be more facilitative versus intervening directly. LEAD activities focus on private sector agro-input suppliers and commodity buyers to generate sustainable benefits for large numbers of smallholder farmers through better, more business-oriented relations with farmers as their customers and suppliers. Employing a light touch facilitation approach to ensure ownershipand therefore sustainability of resultsLEAD provides a combination of technical assistance and cost-sharing (underwriting initial risk of new approaches and technologies) in different combination, encouraging innovations such as developing market entry strategies, assisting early-adopter target firms to scale-up, producing case studies and presentations at industry forums, and hiring field agents to market inputs and to promote and buy high-quality produce. Such successes promote sustainability and encourage emulation by other firms. Coupled with the facilitative value-chain approach, LEAD employs an adaptive planning processcollaboration, learning, adaptationthat allows periodic evaluation of project interventions and gaps, allowing adjustments to the implementation and significantly increasing the effectiveness of the strategy. This built-in learning process allows for quick incorporation of new information and opportunities, which leads to improved project performance and results.

title.narrative: Title II - Development Food Security Activity in Karamoja, Uganda, Nuwoka

description.narrative: FFP supports a USAID Implementing Partner to implement a Development Food Security Activity that builds resilience to shocks, enhances livelihoods, and improves food security and nutrition for an estimated 196,000 people. The Implementing Partner's interventions use an integrated approach that links agricultural and livelihoods activities with the cross-cutting sectors of gender, youth, conflict sensitivity, social accountability, and community ownership.

(Uganda): The Graduating to Resilience activity is a seven year, Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance-funded development food security activity targeting both Congolese refugees and vulnerable Ugandan households in the Kamwenge district of Western Uganda. The activity uses the "graduation into sustainable livelihoods approach"-an intervention that helps extremely poor households overcome multiple deprivations, increase consumption, and develop sustainable livelihoods. The graduation approach is a proven strategy designed to promote economic inclusion through a combination of precise targeting and conditional assistance that is delivered in a series of carefully sequenced interventions. It focuses on building the confidence, capabilities, economic assets, and agency of extremely poor individuals and households in order to improve their resilience to shocks and facilitate their escape from extreme poverty..

title.narrative: Development Innovation Ventures (DIV): Smoothing the Costs of Education: Microsavings in Ugandan Primary Schools

description.narrative: Stage 1: Proof of Concept - Ugandas primary school enrollment rates have increased dramatically as a result of the country's Universal Primary Education strategy, introduced in 1997, which significantly reduced school fees. Unfortunately, even small purchases such as pens and exercise books continue to prevent Ugandan youth from reaching their full potential. As many as 68 percent of enrolled children drop out before completing elementary school, and the majority do so for financial reasons. Innovation for Poverty Action (IPA) and Yale Economist Dean Karlan are conducting research on a Super Savers Program, which encourages students to deposit change into savings boxes to help students and their families save for school fees. The project will help gain a more precise understanding of the financial barriers to high student retention, and how to address them.
